targetText:
When numerous labourers work together side by side, whether in
one and the same process, or in different but connected processes, they
are said to co-operate, or to work in co-operation. [3]
explanation: Co-operation brings many workers together under one roof, creating a collective social power of labor that increases productivity beyond the sum of individual workers.

targetText: Just as the offensive power of a squadron of cavalry, or the defensive power of a regiment of infantry is essentially different from the sum of the offensive or defensive powers of the individual cavalry or infantry soldiers taken separately, so the sum total of the mechanical forces exerted by isolated workmen differs from the social force that is developed, when many hands take part simultaneously in one and the same undivided operation, such as raising a heavy weight, turning a winch, or removing an obstacle.
summary: The collective social power of cooperation: combined labour produces a social force greater than the sum of isolated workers.
explanation: When workers cooperate under a unified plan, their combined collective force generates an enhanced productive power that exceeds the mathematical sum of individual isolated efforts. Under capitalism, this social power of combined labour is appropriated by the capitalist free of charge.
